slice: VS2-R1 B - Original Hunt Loadout evidence closure

authorization.source: Owner directive, 2026-08-28, VS2-R1 Original Gate + Hunt Loadout parity
authorization.scope: VS2-R2: build the Original Hunt Loadout runtime domain from recovered evidence, and publish the implementation-ready contract. No invented item effect. No Capture, no VS3, no Battle, no new save schema.
authorization.finding: The shipped Hunt Loadout is a one-companion selection prototype. The original is a gear / equipment / plugin / launcher system across 11 NXR scenes and 79 catalogued items.
authorization.stopCondition: Runtime and presentation contract complete. Codex rebinds presentation; VS3 Capture is not started.

currentProductStatus.detail: VS2-R2 replaced the companion picker with the recovered structure: five equipment classes and four plugin positions over a Shop-owned inventory, with plugin-gated Hunt HUD capabilities.

companionPrototype.detail: The VS2 companion selection survives as app.selectDeveloperCompanion / app.getDeveloperCompanionCreatureId. It is not on the Player Mode path, the presentation seam does not surface it, it gates nothing, and entering the field never consults it.
companionPrototype.rule: It must never be promoted to Original parity or returned to the Player Mode path.

fieldActor.detail: The Hunt field actor is a product-authored tamer, not a creature the player brought. The original Hunt HUD's creature panel (digimon_name, gen, type, hp, mind, size) describes the WILD target that the Analyzer plugins reveal, so nothing in the evidence supports a companion walking the field.
fieldActor.evidence: PARTIAL - the absence of a companion is evidenced; the tamer avatar itself is product-authored

method.rule: Existing evidence first. Nothing here is inferred from the shipped product UI.
sourcesRead: the 94-scene NXR analysis: scene registry, linked-asset map, and full node tables with coordinates
the UI source-asset, sprite-bundle and background inventories
the ROM-extracted shop catalog with Japanese item names and descriptions
the gameplay master spec, mode-flow map, hunt/capture spec and system-readiness register
method.corroboration: Where a fact is asserted ROM_VERIFIED below it is because two independent artifacts agree - typically an NXR node name and a ROM item string.
method.provenance: All paths are relative to ORIGINAL_EVIDENCE_ROOT, recorded once in research/original-evidence/README.md. No ROM payload, decoded pixel, or machine path enters this repository.

verified.overlay: OVL12 owns both Gate Select and Hunt Loadout.
verified.detail: The mode-flow map states OVL 12 = 'Gate select + Hunt loadout'. Independently, the NXR scene registry attributes all 11 ui/hunt/setting/ scenes AND ui/hunt/world/world_sub_base_scene.nxr to OVL12. Two independent artifacts agree.
verified.romEvidence: The OVL12 -> gate_select/3D_worldMap_model loader call at 0x0210C6FC is a direct code cross-reference; the NXR overlay attribution is inference (SOURCE_LINKED_INFERENCE_FROM_SUBSYSTEM_PATH_AND_PREVIOUS_OVERLAY_TRACE).

documentedFlow.value: Gate Select -> Hunt Loadout -> field -> wild roam/alert/flee -> tools / rope / tether -> circle capture -> capture transaction -> result -> collection
documentedFlow.evidence: PARTIAL - a documented research summary, not a traced call sequence

topMenu.value: Three top-level loadout menus exist as separate scenes: GEAR, PLUGIN, RELEASE.
topMenu.unknown: Their ordering, entry point, and whether EQUIP is a fourth peer or is reached from one of them. `menu_top_release_scene` semantics are UNKNOWN: `release` also appears in hunt_result as release_txt/release_anim, where it plausibly means releasing a captured creature, but the loadout-context meaning is not traced.

unknown: whether loadout is mandatory or skippable

2_elevenNxrSceneRoles.evidence: ROM_VERIFIED at node level; role naming is descriptive
2_elevenNxrSceneRoles.note: Coordinates are NXR node x/y. p6/p7 are the two float params; where they exceed 1.0 they consistently indicate a region extent rather than a scale.

scenes.role: Top-level GEAR menu page. Eight text/dynamic labels over a 12x12 base panel.
Top-level PLUGIN menu page. Eleven text/dynamic labels over the same 12x12 base panel.
Top-level RELEASE menu page. Same shape as the gear page.
EQUIP main screen. Five class touch regions, five plates, five icons, five plate animations, and one large control area.
scenes.layoutNote: The five plates alternate y between 17 and 23 at a 26px x-pitch - a staggered row, not a grid.

scenes.role: EQUIP sub screen. Exactly five equip covers, matching the five classes.
GEAR main screen. Four category tabs with matching touch regions, plus a scrollable list area.
scenes.scrollNote: A dedicated slide area plus its own collision region is direct evidence of a scrollable/draggable list, which is input evidence at the layout level.

scenes.role: GEAR slot strip. Exactly four slots, each with a collision region, a locator and a cover.
scenes.layoutNote: Uniform 19px vertical pitch. Every node is typed SLOT by the analysis.

scenes.role: GEAR sub screen. Exactly four plugin positions, each with a cover.
scenes.layoutNote: The same 19px pitch as the gear slots, at the same x - the gear slot strip and the plugin strip are the two screens of one four-position system.

scenes.role: Item detail panel on the sub screen.
scenes.note: item_desc at 8 x 4 is a four-line description region, which matches the multi-line description strings in the item catalog.

scenes.role: A single item plate with a quantity readout.

quantityFinding.value: num_mul plus exactly two digits is a two-digit quantity readout of the form x NN.
quantityFinding.corroboration: Every consumable Hunt item in the catalog has max_owned = 99. A two-digit field and a 99 cap are the same fact seen from two sides.

scenes.role: Launcher plate frame: a base and a 12x12 background only.

2_elevenNxrSceneRoles.completeness: These are exactly the 11 scenes under ui/hunt/setting/ in the scene registry. No twelfth loadout scene exists.

classes.descriptionSample: A rope for the Baby stage. Durability 10.
classes.note: max_owned 1 and a durability stat: the rope is the single equipped tether, tiered by target evolution stage.

classes.descriptionSample: A gun for stopping a Digimon's movement. Power 10.
classes.note: Ranged immobiliser. Sub-types in the catalog include rapid, sleep, stun and six-round shotgun variants.

classes.descriptionSample: Laid on the ground to block a Digimon's path. Length 24.
classes.note: Ground barrier. Magnet and spark variants exist.

The class name is ROM_VERIFIED from two sides, but which shop subcategories it contains is not traced. Capture Trap ('placed on the ground to capture a Digimon') is the strongest candidate; Meat, Decoy and Light are lures and may belong here or to an untraced class.
Bomb ('deals damage by explosion, power 40') and Mine ('explodes when a Digimon steps on it, power 50') are the strongest candidates. Not traced.

corroboration.finding: The five class names are confirmed independently by ROM item strings, not just by NXR node names.
corroboration.detail: The Plugins/Checker subcategory contains exactly five items whose names are Shot Checker, Wire Checker, Entrap Checker, Damage Trap Checker and All Checker, each described as 'displays the count of <class> items'. Entrap and Damage Trap are therefore first-class in-game item classes in the ROM's own vocabulary, matching col_entrap and col_damage_trap exactly.

huntItemCatalogue.source: shop table base 0x020E0248, stride 0x38 (56 bytes), 118 records

huntSubcategories.name: Decoy
huntSubcategories.role: lure - a walking toy that invites chase

huntSubcategories.name: Light

huntItemCatalogue.resourceKey: Hunt items bind the icon resource key `itemiconL`; plugins bind `setting_obj_plug`, which is the same name as the loadout sprite bundles setting_obj_plug_main / setting_obj_plug_sub.

dayNightConsequence.finding: Both Light items state they can only be used at night.
dayNightConsequence.significance: Day/night is not only a Gate Select presentation state - it gates item usability. This is the first evidence that the day/night pairing in the world map model has a gameplay consequence.
dayNightConsequence.unknown: How the game decides it is night, and whether the Gate Select day/night state selects the Hunt's day/night state.

whatExists.evidence: ROM_VERIFIED that these assets exist and sit inside the Hunt Loadout family

whatIsNotKnown: whether it is equipment, a delivery mechanism for Shot/Bomb/Trap items, or a screen
why it has an associated `wind` sprite
whether it occupies one of the four gear slots

explicitNonEvidence.warning: Do NOT associate this with Desktop_Launcher.nsbmd.
explicitNonEvidence.detail: 3D_DECODED_STRUCTURE lists Launcher_model and Launcher_name nodes, but they belong to battle_menu/Desktop_Launcher.nsbmd and desktop/Desktop_Launcher.nsbmd - the same 38,176-byte file at both paths, identified in the research register (T4) as NDS system-layer UI, not this game's Hunt loadout. The name collision is a trap and is recorded here so it is not walked into.

4_launcherRole.candidateReading: The `wind` companion sprite and the 4-cell icon are consistent with a projectile or delivery device, which would relate it to the Shot class. That is a reading, not evidence, and must not be built on.

5_pluginRole.finding: Plugins are INFORMATION equipment. They do not act on the world; they determine what the Hunt HUD is able to display.

subcategories.name: Checker
subcategories.role: displays remaining counts of an item class

subcategories.name: Radar/Search
subcategories.role: displays creatures on the radar, filtered

analyzerFields.detail: The six single-purpose Analyzer items name exactly the six creature attribute fields present in the Hunt HUD scene, one for one.
analyzerFields.aggregates: Digi-Analyzer alpha (generation + family), beta (generation + family + attribute) and omega ('all stats') are combined analyzers, which is why the HUD has one field set rather than one panel per plugin.
analyzerFields.significance: This is the single most useful loadout finding: the ORIGINAL creature status model shown during a Hunt is generation, family, attribute, HP, personality and capacity - and each field is gated by owning the corresponding plugin.

checkerFields.detail: Four class-specific Checkers - Shot, Wire, Entrap, Damage Trap - correspond exactly to the four remaining-count readouts in the Hunt HUD: remain_icon0..3 with remain_number00..31, four icons each with a two-digit number. The fifth Checker is 'All'.
checkerFields.significance: Four counters and four countable equip classes is the same fact from both directions, and it confirms ROPE is the non-countable fifth class.

radarFields.detail: Radar/Search is the largest plugin subcategory at 15 items, and the sample filters by generation ('displays Baby-stage Digimon on the radar'). The Hunt HUD carries map_marker0..23 - 24 markers - plus map_frame, map_inner_frame and rader_disp_frame.
radarFields.unknown: Whether 24 is a hard contact limit, and what the other 14 radar items filter by.

memoryCheckerField.detail: 'Displays memory card capacity' corresponds to the Hunt HUD nodes mc_cur0, mc_cur1, mc_cur_g, mc_div, mc_max0, mc_max1, mc_max_g - a current/maximum pair, two digits each, with a 'G' unit glyph and a divider.

gearSlots.source: setting_gear_main_slot_scene col_slot0..3 with loc_slot0..3 and slot0..3_cover

6_selectableSlotCounts.reading: Five equipment classes, of which four are countable consumables and one (ROPE) is a single equipped item; and four gear/plugin slots. The gear slot strip and the plugin strip share the same x and the same 19px pitch, so they are the two screens of one four-position system rather than eight positions.
unknown: how many units of a consumable may be taken into a single Hunt
whether the five equip regions are slots to fill or class filters to pick from
whether the four gear slots and four plugin slots are the same four positions viewed on two screens, or two separate sets

7_inventorySource.source: The Shop. Purchases commit to InventoryState at explicit PlayerData offsets recorded per record in the shop catalog.

detail.exampleOffsets: Plugins/Analyzer commit to player offsets 0xAAC, 0xAAE, 0xAB0, 0xAB4 and neighbours - a packed per-item region.
detail.separationRule: InventoryState, CageOwnershipState and ShopVisibilityState are separate domains and must not be merged.
detail.priceRange: 5 Bits for the cheapest consumable up to roughly 90,000 for high-tier ropes; memory cards 2,450-9,850.

7_inventorySource.consequence: The Hunt Loadout does not own an inventory. It presents and selects from a player inventory the Shop writes. Any implementation must read inventory, never mint it.

8_availabilityRules.consequence: Availability is a Shop-side rule keyed on Tamer rank and battle badges, not a Loadout-side rule. The Loadout shows what the player owns; the Shop decides what the player could buy.
8_availabilityRules.note: TAMER_RANK_THRESHOLD is marked HIGH_CONFIDENCE rather than VERIFIED_BINARY in the source catalog. That distinction is preserved here rather than flattened.

9_confirmationFlow.whatIsKnown: setting_equip_main_scene carries a single large interaction region, menu_control_area @(128,102) with extent 16.0 x 9.0, which is the only control-shaped region on the equip screen. setting_gear_main_scene carries slide_area and col_slide_area, evidencing a scrollable list.
whatIsNotKnown: whether a confirmation step exists at all
whether leaving the screen commits or discards
the role of top_mes on the item detail panel
9_confirmationFlow.note: No button node named confirm, ok, decide or cancel exists in any of the 11 scenes. The only node explicitly typed BUTTON anywhere in the Hunt families is close_button in memorycard_plate_scene.

10_loadoutToHuntRuntimeHandoff.finding: The loadout determines the Hunt HUD's capabilities. Every dynamic readout in hunt_sub_scene has a corresponding purchasable plugin.

handoffTable.huntRuntime: gen, type, align_text, hp, mind, size fields plus digimon_name / nick_name / digimon_image_s
remain_icon0..3 and remain_number00..31 - four item-class counters
the capacity value the mc_* readout displays

handoffTable.loadout: Rope / Shot / Wire / Entrap / Damage Trap
handoffTable.huntRuntime: the field tools; the four countable classes drive the remain counters

memoryCardEconomy.detail: Memory Cards state 'lets you hold up to 32G / 64G / 96G captured in a Hunt', and the Memory Analyzer reveals a creature's capacity. Capture capacity is therefore a consumable resource measured in G, spent per captured creature according to that creature's size.
memoryCardEconomy.significance: This is an original Hunt constraint with no equivalent in the current product. It belongs to VS3 Capture, and is recorded here because the loadout is where the capacity is chosen.

unknown: the call that carries the selection into the Hunt runtime
whether the loadout is re-editable mid-Hunt
what happens to unconsumed items on exit

verified: Purchases commit to InventoryState at per-item PlayerData offsets (shop catalog purchase_commit_domain and purchase_commit_player_offset).
Shop visibility persists at PlayerData +0x2F0 with 0/1/2 semantics.
Cage ownership persists in a separate CageOwnershipState domain.
Currency is Bits with a known 9,999,999 cap.
notVerified: whether the SELECTED loadout persists, or only the owned inventory
the complete PlayerData field ledger and the serializer/load chain, which the save-status report states is incomplete
11_savePersistenceRelationship.productRule: Do not copy DS RAM offsets into the shipping schema. The save-status report says so explicitly, and the Championship 2026 envelope is deny-by-default on unknown keys. Any future loadout persistence needs a Claude-owned envelope change and its own authorization; this contract adds no save field.

revisionNote: v1.1 promotes the evidence layer to an implementation-ready contract. VS2-R2 built the runtime domain, so this revision adds the module map, the read-only presentation surface, and the boundary between what was preserved and what is product-authored. No evidence level changed and no unknown was upgraded.

modules.structure: src/championship/hunt/loadout/huntLoadoutContract.js - the recovered constants only. Five classes, per-class rules, plugin kinds, six analyzer fields with their Hunt HUD node names, five checker targets, radar dimensions, three unlock kinds, and the declared unknowns as data.
modules.catalogue: src/championship/hunt/loadout/huntEquipmentCatalog.js - product-authored ITEMS over recovered STRUCTURE. No original item name or description text is present; those are ROM strings and stay in the research tree.
modules.inventory: src/championship/hunt/loadout/huntInventory.js - the Shop-owned boundary. Reads ownership and quantity, evaluates Shop-side availability, and exposes one mutation (grant) that VS4's Shop will own. Nothing in VS2 calls it.
modules.runtime: src/championship/hunt/loadout/huntLoadoutRuntime.js - five class assignments, four plugin positions, validation, confirmation state, derived HUD capabilities and the Hunt handoff.
modules.shell: src/championship/app/vs2Screens.js - a neutral runtime shell rendering the structure. DOM screen UI is Codex's lane; a P1R loadout family replaces it with no runtime change.

preservedExactly: Five equipment classes: ROPE, SHOT, WIRE, ENTRAP, DAMAGE_TRAP.
ROPE caps at one owned and carries a durability value; the other four cap at 99 and are the four the Hunt HUD counts.
Four plugin kinds with their recovered capabilities: Analyzer reveals, Checker counts, Radar shows contacts, Memory Checker shows capacity.
The six analyzer fields and the six Hunt HUD nodes they populate.
Three Shop-side unlock kinds, with TAMER_RANK_THRESHOLD kept at HIGH_CONFIDENCE rather than flattened.
The starting inventory shape from the shop table's initial_owned column: one rope, twenty of the first shot, one memory card, and no plugins.
productAuthoredAndLabelled: Item identities, display names and tier counts. The original's 12 ropes / 12 shots / 6 wires are recorded in this contract, not reproduced.
Numeric stat values. The ROM proves a rope HAS durability and a shot HAS power; it does not say what they do, so the numbers are labels on a scale that nothing consumes.
The empty-loadout rule. No original confirmation requirement is traced, so none is imposed.
deliberatelyAbsent: Per-item runtime effect. Durability, power and length are carried and consumed by nothing.
Any per-Hunt carry limit. Quantity is what is owned, and quantityIsCarryLimit is false.
The launcher, the release menu, and lure class grouping.
Loadout persistence. No save field was added; a test asserts the envelope keys are unchanged.

huntHandoff.carries: the five class assignments with quantity and durability, plus the derived HUD capabilities
huntHandoff.reason: The Hunt runtime receives what is carried, not what it does.

presentationSurface.rule: Presentation sees these fields and nothing else. All are read-only; the named intents are the only mutation route.

frame.huntLoadout.structure: { equipmentClasses: {value 5, evidence ROM_VERIFIED}, pluginPositions: {value 4, evidence ROM_VERIFIED}, positionModel: {value, evidence PARTIAL_HL6_OPEN} }
frame.huntLoadout.availableEquipment: one entry per recovered class: { equipmentClass, countable, maxOwned, statLabel, items: [{ itemId, displayName, tier, quantity, statLabel, statValue, statEffect, durability, selected }] }
frame.huntLoadout.selectedEquipment: one entry per class: { equipmentClass, itemId, displayName, quantity, quantityIsCarryLimit, durability, durabilityConsumption }
frame.huntLoadout.selectedPlugins: four entries: { position, itemId, pluginKind, displayName, capability }
frame.huntLoadout.memoryCard: { itemId, displayName, capacityG, scope } or null
frame.huntLoadout.hudCapabilities: { evidence, analyzerFields, itemCounters, radar, radarFilters, radarMarkerCapacity, memoryReadout, captureCapacityG, captureCapacityScope, note }
frame.huntLoadout.validation: { valid, problems, equippedClassCount, fittedPluginCount, emptyAllowed, emptyAllowedEvidence, note }
frame.huntField.hud.capabilities: the same capability object, so the field renders only what the loadout unlocked

intents.selectEquipment(equipmentClass, itemId |: fill or clear one class; null clears
intents.fitPlugin(position, itemId | null): fit or clear one position; a plugin may occupy only one
intents.beginHunt(): enter the field; gated only on the selection being internally consistent

presentationRules: Render the five recovered classes and four positions. An empty class or position is EMPTY, not disabled: no original rule requires anything to be equipped.
Show quantity for the four countable classes and durability for the rope, because that is the split the ROM makes.
A HUD readout with no plugin behind it is not displayed. That gating is recovered behaviour, not a product choice.
Do not render an item effect, a carry limit, a price, a confirmation requirement, or a companion.
Do not render capture capacity as an action. It is a labelled readout scoped VS3_CAPTURE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
